change: E017_aorta_huwide with loss_fn 'ce_dice': cross-entropy plus a soft Dice term over all five classes, instead of plain cross-entropy. Loss is the only changed variable; the 4-organ target, split, seed, epochs, lr and batch size are identical to E017.
hypothesis: E017's failure mode is systemic under-segmentation of thin/small structures (esophagus predicted/GT volume 0.15-0.60 on every validation patient; Patient_15 aorta 43 % captured). Plain cross-entropy is dominated by the background and penalises a missed thin organ only through per-voxel error, whereas a soft Dice term optimises region overlap directly. Expect esophagus and Patient_15's aorta to improve; the Dice term is averaged over all five classes, and classes absent from both prediction and target contribute roughly zero loss, so the phantom-class artefact of the folded data is not reintroduced.
plan_reference: AORTA_INSPECTION/aorta-findings.md; full_plan.md section 3 (aorta) superseded for a recoverable label

dataset.name: SEGTHOR_aorta_huwide
dataset.source: segthor_part1 (GT class 1 split back into esophagus + aorta)
dataset.label_caveat: Derived, not annotated: the split is validated by Dice 0.9994/0.9980 against the single reference patient (Patient_07 GT2) and by four geometric gates plus visual review on the other 19.

what_to_check: Esophagus 3D Dice against E017's 0.229 and the predicted/GT volume ratio against 0.15-0.60.
Patient_15 aorta against E017's 0.537 (43 % of a 250470-voxel target captured).
Aorta mean against 0.667, heart/trachea against 0.900 / 0.664 - the Dice term must not trade the easy classes away.
check_labels.py --dice_npy: 'main.py:321 mean' must still equal 'mean over classes with GT' (no empty class in the selection mean).
Loss magnitude: CEDiceLoss adds 1 - mean Dice to the CE value, so loss_val.npy is on a different scale than E017's - compare Dice, not loss.

comparison_to_parent.protocol: identical data/split/seed/epochs; the loss is the only changed variable
comparison_to_parent.interpretation: Hypothesis confirmed, and by more than expected. The Dice term roughly doubles the esophagus (0.229 -> 0.428) and lifts the trachea (0.664 -> 0.787) while leaving heart (0.886 vs 0.900) and aorta (0.672 vs 0.667) essentially unchanged. Both thin structures - the two classes that cross-entropy left under-segmented - improve, which is exactly what a region-overlap term predicts. Boundary metrics improve too: heart HD95 36.8 -> 18.8 mm, trachea 57.8 -> 33.2 mm.
comparison_to_parent.under_segmentation_fixed: The predicted/GT volume ratio moves from 0.15-0.60 (E017, every patient under-segmenting) to 0.44-0.92 on three patients and over-segmentation on the two worst (Patient_15 1.86, Patient_19 1.42). The systematic bias is gone; what remains is per-patient localisation error.

notes: Best aorta run so far on fg mean (0.693 vs E017 0.615 and E018 0.606) and the best on the two thin classes.

Patient_15's esophagus is still broken, but the failure changed shape: E017/018 missed it entirely (Dice 0.000, 15-21 % of the target volume), E019 predicts 1.86x the target volume with Dice 0.021, i.e. it now finds plenty of esophagus-shaped tissue in the wrong place. Localisation, not detection.
Heart drops 0.014 against E017 and trachea gains 0.123: the Dice term rebalances capacity toward the small classes, as intended.
Loss scale is not comparable with E017: CEDiceLoss returns CE + (1 - mean Dice), so loss_val.npy is offset by roughly 1. Compare Dice, never loss.
Heart and trachea comparable with every earlier run; esophagus only with runs on data/SEGTHOR_aorta. Labels are derived, not annotated.
